name: Amoxicillin
summary: A broad, commonly used beta-lactam for susceptible respiratory, ENT, dental, and some GI indications.
good: Susceptible community infections when an aminopenicillin is appropriate.
bad: True beta-lactam allergy or clear resistance mismatch.
clinicalPearls: Common does not mean universal — local resistance still decides whether it works.
mechanism: Beta-lactam inhibition of PBPs blocks bacterial cell-wall cross-linking.
indications: ENT infections, streptococcal infections, dental infections, and H. pylori combination regimens.
interactionNotes: Clavulanate extends beta-lactamase coverage when used in combination; all beta-lactams need allergy review.

warnings: Penicillin allergy, diarrhea, and resistance-limited empiric use are the main issues.
